stories.headline: Paraguay’s Congress rejects president’s resignation amid banking crisis

sources.body:
Lawmakers are advancing impeachment proceedings against Pena, questioning his ties to the digital lender Ueno.

Paraguay’s Congress has refused to accept President Santiago Pena’s resignation, pressing ahead with impeachment proceedings after the collapse of digital lender Ueno Bank.

President since 2023, Pena had attempted to resign on Thursday as millions of Ueno customers remained unable to access their accounts.

“I do so with the stability of our country, social peace and the need to preserve our democratic institutions in mind,” the conservative politician said in a recorded address.

But lawmakers declined to accept his resignation. The lower house voted 78-0 to impeach him, and the Senate opened impeachment proceedings, summoning him to appear on Friday.

A joint congressional session called to consider the resignation lost its quorum after lawmakers from Pena’s Colorado Party walked out, as it became clear there were not enough votes to accept it.

Horacio Cartes, a leader in the Colorado Party, had posted a statement on social media indicating the group supported Pena’s impeachment.

“We will not side with the theft of public, private and pension funds,” Cartes, a former president, wrote in his statement. “We must think of the people and the values we uphold in the Colorado Party.”

Denying Pena’s resignation is likely to heighten the legal jeopardy he faces.

Ordinarily, in Paraguay, presidents who leave office become senators for life, and they enjoy a degree of legal immunity from prosecution as members of the legislature.

But that status is not conferred if the president is convicted in an impeachment trial.

The political crisis erupted earlier this week, when Paraguay’s central bank announced that Ueno had fallen below the legal solvency ratio. Once its books were corrected, the bank’s capital – the cushion banks must keep to absorb losses – was less than half the legal minimum.

Before its collapse, the company claimed it had about 3 million customers, in a country of 6.5 million people. Many have since lost access to their accounts and to pensions paid out through the bank.

As part of a resolution to address the bank’s collapse, Paraguay’s central bank voted to transfer its remaining funds to other financial institutions.

But the central bank itself came under scrutiny for not properly regulating Ueno. The central bank’s head, Carlos Carvallo, has since resigned.

Pena himself formerly held a stake in Ueno’s parent company, Grupo Vazquez, though he said he sold those shares in 2025.

Lawmakers, however, have accused Pena of having a conflict of interest and have questioned whether there was an institutional cover-up linked to the lender’s collapse.

“He is accused of negligence at the very least and complicity in covering up the fact that the bank was insolvent,” said Al Jazeera’s Latin America editor Lucia Newman.

“As I speak, there are people outside urging Congress not to accept the resignation of the president because they say that they want him tried and impeached.”
sources.headline: Paraguay Congress rejects President Pena’s resignation after bank collapse

sources.body: Paraguay’s lower house voted unanimously to impeach President Santiago Peña on Thursday, just minutes after he announced his resignation on X. Protesters have rallied in the streets since the takeover of a bank linked to Peña blocked millions of people, including pensioners, from accessing their money.
sources.headline: Paraguay's president Peña impeached moments after resigning over banking scandal

stories.headline: Israel’s Arab Joint List backs Eisenkot to form a government

sources.body:
Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats in Israel’s 120-seat parliament in last week’s general election.

The Joint List alliance of Arab-led parties says it will back Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form a new government after last week’s election.

“The Joint List announced today, Thursday, that it will inform the President of the State, Isaac Herzog, this evening of its decision to recommend that Gadi Eisenkot be tasked with forming the government,” the alliance said in a statement.

Arab-led parties won a record 19 seats in Israel’s 120-seat parliament in last week’s general election, a result that could give them significant influence over the formation of the next government.

Once the Joint List’s 11 lawmakers formally submit their recommendation, Eisenkot is expected to have the backing of 67 lawmakers, exceeding the 61-seat majority threshold in the Knesset.

Earlier, Ra’am, an Arab-led party with eight seats, said it would also recommend Eisenkot.

Meanwhile, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc with 53 seats may not yield 53 endorsements, as Degel HaTorah, which holds four of United Torah Judaism’s seven seats, said it would recommend neither candidate.

The ultra-Orthodox faction broke with Netanyahu over his coalition’s failure to pass legislation exempting Haredi men from military service, The Times of Israel reported.

Netanyahu has also claimed repeatedly and without evidence that Arab parties committed fraud during the elections with foreign backing.

The prime minister and his Likud party have cited a handful of cases, including the arrests of three political activists who allegedly bribed voters before polls opened. They are suspected of connections with the Ra’am party, although the party denies any involvement.

Netanyahu and Likud also suggested that the opposition bloc joining with Arab-led parties would be treasonous. In a statement after the vote, Likud warned that Zionist parties cooperating with the Arab bloc would be “dangerous to Israel”.

Israel’s Central Elections Committee certified the results of the election on Wednesday after finding no evidence of fraud.

President Herzog has also accepted the results and begun consultations with party leaders on whom to task with forming the next government.

He also backed investigating suspected interference but warned against smearing voters who are Palestinian citizens of Israel, saying he had “great respect” for the country’s Palestinian minority, which makes up about 20 percent of the population.

“I condemn the coarseness and racist expressions that we have heard recently,” he said.

On Wednesday, the president said he had met representatives of the Religious Zionism and Zehut, Shas and Yisrael Beytenu factions.

In a post on X, Herzog said he “received their recommendations regarding the identity of the Knesset member upon whom the task of forming the government should be assigned”.

Herzog added that talks would also continue on Thursday.

Once the consultations end, Herzog will choose the candidate he considers best placed to assemble a coalition, almost certainly Netanyahu or Eisenkot. He has several days to announce his decision, after which the nominee will have 28 days to form a government, with a possible 14-day extension.
sources.headline: Joint List says it will back Eisenkot to form Israel’s next government

sources.body: Israel's largest Arab party grouping said Thursday it would recommend opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, potentially bolstering his bid after Arab-majority lists won a record 19 seats in last week's election and Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu lost the support of an allied religious party.
sources.headline: Israel's Arab list backs Eisenkot as Netanyahu loses ultra-Orthodox support

stories.headline: Hoax bomb threats disrupt dozens of flights across Europe

sources.body:
Planes forced into emergency landings or diversions two days after hoax alerts affected air travel

Why have more than 30 European flights been hit by bomb threats this week?

Hoax bomb threats have disrupted at least 34 flights across Europe this week, with some forced to make emergency landings, as questions mount over an apparently coordinated effort to cause chaos for travellers.

At least 25 bomb threats affected flights on Thursday between Italy, Ireland, the UK, Spain, Bulgaria, Romania, Poland, Finland, Austria, Denmark, Belgium, Portugal, France, Greece, Serbia and Czechia.

The threats affected flights by Ryanair, Aer Lingus, Wizz Air, Finnair, easyJet, Aegean Airlines, Iberia, Sky Express, Air Serbia and LOT Polish Airlines. All landed safely. Searches of the planes found nothing suspicious.

In the UK, Heathrow, London’s principal airport, and Birmingham airport received threats overnight, but it was determined that they were hoaxes with the help of specialist investigators from the Metropolitan police’s aviation police command.

The Met said threats had been made against four aircraft departing from or arriving at Heathrow. A police spokesperson added that, after an assessment, “no security issues [were] identified”.

The day of hoaxes followed similar threats on Tuesday, when seven planes across Europe were searched or diverted after malicious alerts. On Monday a flight from the UK to Bulgaria was diverted after a threat that was apparently without substance.

Investigators said on Thursday there remained no evidence that the hoaxes were being orchestrated by a hostile terror group or state actor, such as Russia or Iran, although inquiries across Europe into the incidents continue.

The global airlines body Iata condemned the disruption and urged authorities to identify the origin of the threats. “Safety is the number one priority for the industry and we take all threats seriously,” said Nick Careen, Iata’s senior vice-president for operations, safety and security, in a statement.

The EU transport commissioner, Apostolos Tzitzikostas, said it was too early to know if the incidents were linked but that any threats against civilians were unacceptable.

Bomb threats emailed to airports in Rome and Sofia were signed “fighters of the Male State”, according to sources at Aeroporti di Roma, which manages the city’s two airports, and a text seen by Agence France-Presse.

Male State is a Russian far-right, ultranationalist and misogynistic movement founded in 2016 by Vladislav Pozdnyakov. On his Telegram channel Pozdnyakov, a prominent supporter of the war in Ukraine, did not comment on or claim responsibility for the bomb threats.

The emails reportedly read: “We, the fighters of the Male State, will make history with our actions today. Your feminist regime will remember this for ever. The explosion will occur in 60 minutes. Today, your skies will turn red.”

A Cork airport spokesperson confirmed to the Guardian that the airport had received an anonymous threat by phone on Thursday morning, causing a flight to be delayed. It was understood to be a Ryanair flight from London Stansted.
sources.headline: Bomb threats disrupt dozens of flights across Europe, raising hybrid war fears

sources.body: Hoax bomb threats hit at least 27 affected flights around Europe this week.
sources.headline: Europe: Dozens of flights diverted following bomb threats

stories.headline: Hundreds of thousands protest across France over living costs

sources.body:
Hundreds of thousands demonstrate over cost of living and cuts to public services as 70,000 police officers deployed

Hundreds of thousands of people have marched in cities across France in the latest round of street demonstrations, as trade unions put pressure on the government with a general strike over the cost of living and cuts to public services.

Striking teachers, hospital staff and rail workers joined high school and university students in largely peaceful demonstrations in Paris and other cities on Thursday amid a high police presence of 70,000 officers.

The government estimated that at least 600,000 people had taken part, while the leftwing CGT trade union put the figure at almost 1.6 million.

Riot police fired teargas at the end of demonstrations in Bordeaux and Lyon. In Paris, police prevented schoolchildren from setting up barricades with wheelie bins outside high schools across the city in the early morning.

In the east of the city, police used teargas to prevent students from accessing the Hélène Boucher high school.

“This is a historic protest movement but the government’s only real response has been to seriously crack down on it with police, so we had to come out on to the street today,” said Rebecca, 30, a social worker for children with disabilities from Paris’s southern suburbs. “There are police everywhere, but where is the funding for other public services?”

Emmanuel Macron’s final months in office continue to be marred by domestic crises, as high school students protesting over poor learning conditions have been joined by workers in weekly protests .

Meanwhile, the government is struggling to pass a belt-tightening budget in a divided parliament as public debt approaches 120% of economic output.

France’s four main rail unions said the government’s proposed budget cuts would “worsen poverty, slash social security, freeze state workers’ salaries and dry up investment needed for environmental measures”.

Amid the renewed protests centred on living costs, public spending cuts and the troubled education system, the far-right, anti-immigration presidential candidate Marine Le Pen is polling high for the 2027 election to replace Macron next spring.

High school students, who have been protesting for weeks, continued to blockade schools over overcrowded classes and dilapidated buildings, saying the government’s proposed measures on capping some class sizes and loaning funds to regional authorities to fix schools were not enough. The government said 81 high schools were affected on Thursday, while students’ unions put the number at 1,000.

University students joined in blockading faculties, with a third of higher education sites affected, the government said. Trade unions from across the political landscape joined strikes, with private school teacher unions taking part alongside state school teachers.

At the Paris demonstration, a 46-year-old psychiatric nurse from the city’s south-eastern suburbs said: “We’ve got to protect public services. Hospital cuts are impacting the work we try to do with psychiatric patients.
sources.headline: Protesters march in cities across France as unions stage general strike

stories.headline: Three in four displaced people live in countries highly exposed to climate hazards, UN says

sources.body: Nearly 90 million forcibly displaced people, or three-quarters of the global total, live in countries highly exposed to climate hazards, the UN refugee agency said on Friday, urging action ahead of the COP31 climate summit in Turkey. It said droughts, floods and extreme heat were making lasting solutions harder to find.
sources.headline: Three in four displaced people live in climate danger zones, UN says

stories.headline: California governor commutes all 548 death sentences to life without parole

sources.body: California Governor Gavin Newsom on Thursday said he would commute all 548 death sentences in the state to life in prison without parole, marking a major step away from capital punishment as he prepares to leave office after eight years.
sources.headline: 'Inhumane punishment': Governor Gavin Newsom to commute all 548 California death sentences

sources.body:
Gavin Newsom cites concerns over morality, high costs, human error as he grants largest mass clemency in US history.

California Governor Gavin Newsom has announced that he will commute the sentences of all 548 people on death row in the state, the largest mass clemency in United States history.

The announcement on Thursday effectively clears out California’s death row , although the state has not executed a prisoner for 20 years. Those on death row will instead serve life sentences without the possibility of parole.

“I take this action because I firmly believe that state-sanctioned killing is incompatible with California’s values, undermines the foundations of our legal system, and diminishes each of us,” Newsom said in an open letter.

Support for the death penalty in the US has largely declined since the 1990s, although it still holds majority backing.

A Pew Research Center poll released in August found that 66 percent of Americans supported the punishment for those convicted of murder. Roughly 73 percent, however, acknowledged there was a risk of executing an innocent person.

Because death penalty cases often involve long and arduous legal appeals, many of those on death row are never executed.

Twenty-three states have banned the practice outright, and others have effectively abandoned it even if the punishment remains on the books.

Still, President Donald Trump, a Republican, has championed the death penalty for serious federal crimes. In April, his administration pledged to expand the use of federal executions, including by employing firing squads.

While proponents of the death penalty have argued that the punishment has a deterrent effect, critics say decades of scholarship indicate otherwise.

They have also pointed to ethical and logistical issues, including the expense.

According to the Death Penalty Information Center (DPIC), California has spent $6bn on the death penalty since 1978 while carrying out just 13 executions in that time.

Capital punishment has also been criticised for being applied disproportionately to racial minorities and for the frequency of botched executions .

The DPIC says that, since 1973, at least 203 people wrongly convicted and sentenced to death in the US have later been exonerated.

Newsom’s decision has been praised by criminal justice groups as a step away from a practice they say is outdated, inefficient and immoral.

“Governor Newsom’s announcement marks a decisive moment in the history of the death penalty in the United States. Though other governors have granted universal clemencies, none have been at this scale,” Robin Maher, the executive director of the DPIC, said in a statement.

“By bookending his time as governor first with a moratorium and now this mass clemency, Governor Newsom has irrevocably changed California’s relationship with the death penalty.”

The DPIC noted that about two-thirds of the commutations must be reviewed by the California Supreme Court, which is required under state law to review clemency for anyone with multiple felony convictions, before they become final.
sources.headline: California governor commutes sentences of more than 500 people on death row

stories.headline: AI stocks fall as investors assess the US election and slowing growth

sources.body:
Tech stocks lead US market slide as investors weigh impact of midterm election results on AI industry.

United States markets slid on Thursday, with losses in US chip and data centre-related stocks fuelling pressure on the technology sector following Democrats’ sweeping midterm election wins.

The tech-heavy Nasdaq was down 4.8 percent in midday trading, while the S&P 500 fell 3.6 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average slid 2.8 percent.

US markets jumped on Wednesday following the midterm election , with Democrats’ sweeping wins signalling limits on policy shocks from a Congress at odds with the White House. Markets were also reassured by US President Donald Trump’s remarks that he would accept the election results.

Artificial intelligence (AI) stocks – which have driven much of the market’s growth – led the plunge in the tech sector that drove down markets on Thursday.

Of the 45 data centre ballot initiatives around the country, voters backed restrictions on most of them. According to Data Centers on the Ballot, 39 ballot measures to restrict AI were successful, while only one — in North Dakota — voted against restrictions.

UBS analysts estimated that potential construction pauses could put roughly 30 percent of planned US data centre capacity additions in 2028 at risk, according to the Reuters news agency.

“Yesterday, markets rallied on certainty as election results removed a layer of uncertainty. Today, portfolio managers and analysts are digging into the implications and adjusting expectations for potential political resistance to AI infrastructure, particularly at the state and local levels,” Michael Monaghan, portfolio manager of Founders 100 ETF, told Al Jazeera.

“We’re seeing that concern reflected in the selloff across semiconductors and hyperscalers.”

Data centre operators and neocloud companies were slumping, with CoreWeave down over 12 percent and Nebius Group down nearly 17 percent. Semiconductor stocks such as AI market leader Nvidia fell by 8.2 percent, Micron by nearly 14 percent and Intel by 6.8 percent in midday trading.

AI server manufacturer Dell dropped nearly 13 percent.

Other tech giants were also in negative territory, with Amazon falling 2 percent and Facebook and Instagram’s parent company, Meta, down 3.8 percent.

SpaceX also took a big hit, with shares down 9.5 percent, while Tesla, also owned by billionaire Elon Musk, fell over 11 percent, following Musk’s nearly half-billion-dollar midterm election spending spree.

In Texas, where both companies are headquartered, Musk bet against Democratic candidates who ended up winning their races. Musk shelled out $230m to defeat US Senate candidate James Talarico, $5m to back Gina Hinojosa’s opponent in the governor’s race and $500,000 in the lieutenant governor’s race, which Democrat Vikki Goodwin won.

“We will believe a SpaceX/Tesla merger happens but now faces a much tougher regulatory roadmap to get this deal done in 2027 given this new political blue roadmap in DC/Texas,” Dan Ives, managing partner of Yorkville Ives, said in a note on Thursday.
sources.headline: AI stocks plunge after US election, driving down markets

sources.body:
Traders en Wall Street, en una imagen de archivo

Bienvenidos a la montaña rusa de los mercados de la segunda parte... del segundo mandato de Donald Trump. Las tecnológicas se desplomaron este jueves en Wall Street, después de las ganancias del día anterior, cuando los mercados celebraron la victoria demócrata en las urnas. Como suele ocurrir, pasada la resaca de las fiestas, de repente se vuelve a la realidad. De la promesa de la IA ya hemos pasado a la narrativa del coste de la IA.

Los inversores temen que con el nuevo curso político aumenten las restricciones a los centros de datos o que el marco normativo pase a ser más exigente. Y con menos inversiones, habría menos pedidos para chips y otros componentes de la cadena productiva.

A media tarde del jueves la Bolsa de Nueva York sufría una auténtica sangría. El índice Nasdaq 100, el que agrupa a las mayores compañías del sector, caía un 5%. Por su parte, el SP500, el más representativo de Wall Street resbalaba más del 3% y el Dow Jones Industriales perdía cerca del 2%. Las empresas de semiconductores registraban a su vez un descenso del 11%, con Nvidia recortando cerca del 8%. Por su parte, Qualcomm anunció unos resultados decepcionantes y se anotó su mayor retroceso en seis años. Fue la gota que colmó el vaso.

Las llamadas siete magníficas, las joyas de la corona del big tech, vivieron en conjunto una hemorragia difícil de contener: su capitalización bursátil se vio recortada en más de 1 billón de dólares, lo que representaría la segunda mayor caída registrada en un solo día. Tesla fue el vagón de cola, con un desplome que rondaba el 10%.

¿Está justificada esta reacción? Los demócratas pueden bloquear nuevas propuestas legislativas de la Casa Blanca, negociar condiciones y utilizar los poderes de investigación. Pero el resultado electoral no cancela automáticamente las decisiones ya tomadas.

Aún así, los centros de datos despiertan malestar. Consumen electricidad y agua, producen ruido y requieren nuevas infraestructuras. Las comunidades locales se preguntan qué beneficios reciben a cambio y quién paga las intervenciones en la red. Según una encuesta a pie de urna de la NBC, la mayoría de los votantes señala los centros de datos como un factor crucial en su decisión de voto. Según Goldman Sachs, este nuevo cuadro político puede afectar al 45% de los proyectos de expansión programados. Los cinco estados donde más se construyen estas instalaciones a partir de ahora estarán en manos de gobiernos demócratas. Los analistas de UBS estimaron que alrededor del 30% de las incorporaciones de capacidad de centros de datos previstas en EE.UU. para 2028 podrían estar en riesgo debido a posibles pausas en la construcción.

Desde la gestora Pimco, Libby Cantrill, director de asuntos públicos, cree que estos temores de los inversores son reales. “La opinión predominante parece ser que las declaraciones contra los centros de datos responden únicamente a la retórica propia de un año electoral, pero a los nuevos gobernadores les resultará difícil incumplir sus compromisos electorales y no imponer, como mínimo, determinadas restricciones a los centros de datos, cuando no moratorias completas. Una ralentización del desarrollo de estas infraestructuras podría ejercer presiones a la baja sobre el crecimiento económico, la inflación y los tipos de interés”.
sources.headline: El freno demócrata a los centros de datos congela la euforia de las bolsas

stories.headline: Progressives point to economic populism after Democratic midterm victories

sources.body: In 2016, two populist revolutions threatened to remake American politics. Donald Trump’s conquered the Republican Party and delivered him the presidency. Bernie Sanders’ fell short against Hillary Clinton but introduced a populist economic vision that, at the time, much of the Democratic establishment dismissed as politically impractical. Ten years later, Trump and MAGA were hit with a devastating midterm repudiation, as candidates across the country in blue and red states echoing versions of Sanders' message broke through in places that once seemed beyond Democrats' reach. Sanders, as cantankerous as ever, isn’t surprised. “If you're asking me, am I shocked by that? That the argument about economic justice and taking on oligarchs and fighting for the working class is working in Texas, is working in Ohio, is working in Montana, is working in Florida, is working all over the country — no, I am not shocked,” Sanders said in an interview Wednesday, fresh off over 20 rallies in October alone. “That is what I’ve always believed.” Sanders’ laser focus on economic populism in 2016 faced criticism from his own party during his contentious primary against Clinton for being too dismissive of identity politics — often couched as his lack of support among Black voters. Now, his brand of relentless focus on corporate and billionaire election interventions and income inequality proved a winning formula not only for Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, but for James Talarico in Texas, Sam Forstag in Montana and Rebecca Cooke in Wisconsin. “Bernie normalized the kind of campaigning that really is about making a direct appeal to working people,” El Sayed told POLITICO. “Wherever I went in Michigan, there are people who remember Bernie 2016 and Bernie 2020 — we stand on the shoulders of giants.” Given the booming results Tuesday and the breadth of wins for the left, Democrats will test whether they can avoid the same pitfalls that ultimately dogged them following their last major win in 2020 with Joe Biden’s blue-collar charm at the top of the ticket, after which the party gradually slipped back down the culture war slope. To avoid that, Sanders said the party can do both, but that Democrats need to have the “courage” to focus on the day-to-day needs of working families, no matter what the billionaires funding the Democratic Party say. “It's not either or. You can fight against bigotry and discrimination, but you have got to have the courage,” he said. “The courage now to say to the billionaires who are funding the Democratic Party: ‘Thank you very much for your help, but right now we are going to focus on the needs of the working families of this country, whether you like it or not.’” Sanders’ reach is perhaps nowhere more evident than in New York City, which has emerged as the mecca of American progressivism, where Mayor Zohran Mamdani — once a Sanders-endorsed local official — is now perhaps the heir-apparent to Sanders’ progressive mantle. The man behind Mamdani's seismic rise, progressive wunderkind Morris Katz, had more than most on the line this week. After his top client Graham Platner dropped out of the Senate race in Maine earlier this year amid scandal, Katz worked this cycle for Gina Hinojosa in Texas, Randy Villegas in California and Brian Poindexter in Ohio, while his firm, Fight Agency, worked with El-Sayed and Pennsylvania’s Bob Brooks. The day before the election, The Atlantic published a 3,500-word piece that put “Katz’s theory of politics” on the ballot. “A lot of people wanted to know what I’d say if we lost,” Katz said, referencing an infamous Kanye West quote Wednesday and running on 45 minutes of sleep. “I guess we’ll never know. That’s about how I feel today.” Like Sanders, Katz sees a progressive future laser-focused on economics as the clear way forward — and nowhere is that more clear than in Texas. “Hundreds of millions were spent against James and Gina trying to tag them on a trans issue,” he said. “It failed in epic fashion because there was no room for misunderstanding or ambiguity over what they stood for, because they had grounded themselves in such affirmative and positive economic messaging.” “Those attacks have succeeded in the absence of an affirmative message,” he added. “Once you’re able to define yourself and provide a message, it's just a lot harder for that to work.” It's the same formula Mamdani rode to Gracie Mansion — and, Katz argues, the lesson Democrats finally absorbed. “For a long time, politicians accepted the realities of how people felt about the economy but refused responsibility for having to take an active role in changing it,” he said. “There's no room for that anymore.” Katz sees his and Sanders’ theory of politics as having won out across the Democratic spectrum — not just on the left flank, but among the moderates who once resisted it. “The more moderate wing of the party has changed the definition of what a moderate is. I think that’s great,” he said. “We should be a big tent party, but you are seeing a big tent that is unified in opposition to the oligarchy, that is unified in opposition to corruption, and that is united in a pursuit of fundamental and structural change. And that’s going to be really encouraging if that can carry over to 2028.” For Sanders, it’s vindication of an argument he's made for years and that Democrats have ignored — despite what he says is its simplicity. “Focusing on the needs of the vast majority of American people who are struggling in the richest country on earth, while the very rich are getting richer, man, you don't need a Ph.D. in economics or political science to figure that out,” he said. “That is the issue. How do we create a decent standard of living for all of our people? How do we end the corrupt campaign finance system? That is exactly what Democrats have got to do.” At 85, Sanders campaigned this cycle like a man running out of time. In the wake of Trump’s historic return to power in 2024, Sanders launched the “Fighting Oligarchy” tour, which came when many democrats were on the sidelines but provided a lot of the arguments, and even helped discover actual candidates who a year later would swamp races earlier this week. Since the tour, Sanders has held 58 rallies during the midterms, endorsed more than 150 candidates across the primaries and general election, spent north of $16 million on organizing and deployed staff and volunteers into key Senate states including Michigan, Minnesota and Florida, an adviser to Sanders told POLITICO. “People say, ‘you know, Bernie, you’re not 21 years of age. What keeps you going?’” Sanders said. “What keeps me going is you look at the people who we have just elected yesterday, and look at the hundreds of other people who we have elected in school board and city council. You have wonderful people, black and white and Latino, coming from rural areas, urban areas.” “I hope the Democratic leadership has seen what's happening around the country,” he added. Looking ahead to 2028, progressives see Tuesday as evidence the left’s economic politics can win anywhere — and that any doubt from moderates that a progressive should run for president should be laid to rest. “I think we’ve got to rethink politics,” Sanders said. “We can win over millions of Republicans and independents who are struggling economically if we focus on the issues that are important,” he added, pointing to Villegas in Bakersfield, “a Republican town,” along with Forstag, Cooke and others who flipped Republican-held seats. “These are people who ran on a progressive agenda, taking on a Republican district, and they won,” he said. Katz said Tuesday was proof that heading into 2028, voters want candidates who look nothing like Washington — the kind he's helped elect from Texas to California. “You saw a hunger for a different kind of candidate — on congressional [level], teachers and waitresses and firefighters and iron workers and smokejumpers. And on the Senate level, pastors and doctors and teachers,” he said. “This hunger for expanding who is in Congress, who's in the positions of power, feels real.” What progressive candidate can pick up the left’s momentum heading into 2028 remains a question, but Katz said he viewed Tuesday’s results as more evidence that New York Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez — who closed out Villegas’ campaign in California a week before the election and stumped in Michigan, Montana and Pennsylvania — should consider running for president. “You’d be hard pressed to look at the results of the election and say they're anything other than encouraging in the context of her ability to win nationwide,” Katz said. Lisa Kashinsky contributed to this report.
sources.headline: Bernie Sanders lost the fight in 2016. A decade later, he won the war.

stories.headline: Abdul El-Sayed ran behind other Michigan Democrats in heavily Jewish communities

sources.body: Abdul El-Sayed ran well behind other Michigan Democrats in places with more Jewish voters, according to a detailed POLITICO analysis of precinct-level results. Statewide, the progressive senator-elect only ran two points behind Democratic Gov.-elect Jocelyn Benson, getting 52.5% of the vote compared to her 54.5%. But the gap was much larger in heavily Jewish communities: In Huntington Woods, a Detroit suburb that is roughly two-thirds Jewish, El-Sayed ran nearly 15 points behind Benson, getting 65.3% of the vote compared to Benson’s 80%. In West Bloomfield, the site of the March synagogue attack that shook the Senate primary and a town where roughly a quarter of residents are Jewish, El-Sayed ran 8.8 points behind Benson. El-Sayed faced blowback from some Jewish Democrats during his campaign, particularly over his calls to end U.S. military support to Israel and his remarks after the synagogue attack that “hurt people hurt people,” for which he later apologized . El-Sayed, who will be the first Muslim senator in U.S. history, told POLITICO on Wednesday that he hoped he could “earn support” from Jewish voters who hadn’t backed him in this election. “One of the big issues of disagreement that kept showing up when it came to the Jewish community was my position on Israel,” El-Sayed said. “I'm not going to change my position, but …I intend to lead on all the issues that we agree on — whether it's the right to a union or the right to health care, clean air, clean water, or religious pluralism, and respect for the Constitution — and I hope that over time I can earn [their] support on those issues.” El-Sayed had worked to make inroads with Jewish voters over the course of his campaign, pledging to stand up to antisemitism and for Jewish safety. Still, some Jewish leaders and activists in the state urged voters to blank their ballots in the Senate race, or back Republican former Rep. Mike Rogers. His former Democratic primary rival, Rep. Haley Stevens, also switched her endorsement from El-Sayed to Rogers days before the election, citing concerns over antisemitism and the Democrat and his allies’ views and rhetoric around Israel. She pointed to an ad put out by a prominent El-Sayed supporter tying high grocery prices to U.S. aid to Israel, which El-Sayed and his campaign distanced themselves from. Jewish voters, who make up roughly 1.4% of the Michigan electorate, have historically backed Democrats by large margins. But disagreements over support for Israel and how the party should respond to rising antisemitism are testing that voting bloc — both in Michigan and across the country. A poll of Jewish early voters in the state found that a majority still backed El-Sayed, but roughly one in four who had supported Sen. Elissa Slotkin in 2024 switched to back Rogers. With Michigan in Democrats’ early primary window for 2028, El-Sayed said his statewide win showed voters were aligned with his positioning on Israel — and that he hopes the next presidential nominee takes note. “If you want to be where the voters are, if you want to be on the side of peace and on the side of justice and transparency, I believe that that is around holding Israel accountable to its war crimes and on making sure our tax dollars get used to do good things here rather than bad things somewhere else,” he said. In a post-election memo , El-Sayed’s campaign touted an outside analysis finding that he only ran slightly behind Slotkin’s 2024 performance in predominantly Jewish precincts. The memo also noted he was outspent heavily in both the primary and general elections, including by “MAGA billionaires, AIPAC, Elon Musk, and corporate interests determined to elect candidates who would defend the status quo.” But he won in a blue wave while Slotkin, who is Jewish, overcame a tough year. El-Sayed’s margins were far better than Slotkin’s numbers across nearly all of the state, suggesting Jewish voters moved in the opposite direction of most Michiganders. On the other hand, El-Sayed particularly surged in areas with more Muslim voters, who make up roughly 2.4% of Michigan’s electorate. In Dearborn, for example, he won 82.5% of the vote compared to 78.7% for Benson. Two years ago, Slotkin won 41.4% in the city while former Vice President Kamala Harris received just 36.3% of the vote. Lansing Mayor Andy Schor, a Jewish Democrat who supported Stevens in the primary and did not endorse El-Sayed, said he was unsurprised by that split screen. He expressed hope about El-Sayed’s relationship with the Jewish community going forward, but also said Jewish leaders should continue to raise their concerns to the incoming senator. “Everybody has to keep talking to him. His views aren’t going to change, and we know what they are,” Schor said. But, “I hope he’s open to hearing the concerns of some of his constituents.” Nonnegotiable Michigan, a group of Jewish activists that pushed El-Sayed on issues of Jewish safety and Israel, also said in a postelection statement that it was “prepared to work with” El-Sayed “even as we continue to hold elected leaders accountable when antisemitism enters our politics or political discourse.” El-Sayed made clear he has no plans to change his views on Israel, but said he will be straight with voters — and that he’ll “show up for you when you need me” regardless of their differences. “With me, what you see is what you get. And I've never once gone and told somebody that I was anything but what I am,” El-Sayed said Wednesday. “We're going to disagree. I'm going to be honest, specific and direct. And over time, I hope that I can earn support for leading on the issues on which I hope to lead and [by] serving everybody.”

Parte del operativo se ha desarrollado en Valencia, donde efectivos del instituto armado han registrado el domicilio del exministro, en prisión tras ser condenado por el Tribunal Supremo por las irregularidades en la compra de mascarillas durante lo peor de la pandemia. sources.headline: La UCO registra la casa de Ábalos en Valencia en un nuevo operativo del ‘caso Koldo’ con seis detenidos

sources.body:
Agentes de la Unidad Central Operativa (UCO) de la Guardia Civil han registrado este jueves el domicilio en Valencia del exministro José Luis Ábalos y también han realizado requerimiento de documentos en la sede de Adif Alta Velocidad, en el marco de una operación relacionada con las investigaciones sobre la trama Koldo según han confirmado a EL PERIÓDICO fuentes cercanas a la investigación.

Las actuaciones se enmarcan en una nueva pieza de carácter secreto abierta el pasado martes por el juez que investiga este caso en la Audiencia Nacional, Ismael Moreno, que se han saldado por el momento con seis detenciones de carácter policial, entre ellas la de la actual pareja de Ábalos, Andrea de la Torre, el que fuera chófer del PSOE Cristian Corvillo, su hermano Rubén y otros tres empresarios. Todos ellos fueron quedando en libertad una vez que se les tomó declaración y se practicaron las diligencias previstas. El magistrado les citará a declarar en la Audiencia Nacional más adelante.

Según una resolución del magistrado a la que tuvo acceso esta redacción, la nueva pieza de investigación se abrió tras recibir un informe procedente de la Unidad de Delincuencia Económica de la UCO y los requerimientos tendrían que ver con la información contenida en este documento . El delito que aparece en la resolución es el de estafa a lo que se añade "todos los supuestos".

Fuentes de la Fiscalía Anticorrupción apuntan a presuntos delitos de organización criminal, blanqueo y tráfico de influencias , mientras que desde la defensa de Ábalos reprochan que se trate de una investigación paralela sobre hechos ya enjuiciados, lo que consideran un disparate jurídico dirigido a “hacer más daño gratuito”.

La operación, en la que también participa la Fiscalía Anticorrupción, ha motivado la personación de agentes de la UCO en dependencias de Adif "con una solicitud de información", confirman fuentes de esta entidad pública. Añaden que desde el Administrador de Infraestructuras Ferroviarias se ha prestado total colaboración atendiendo a dicha petición de información, y que no se ha practicado registro alguno en estas dependencias.

En el transcurso de la operación se produjeron varias detenciones y los agentes centraron las entradas y registros ordenadas por el juez en Valencia, Madrid, Córdoba y Sevilla, donde los agentes se personaron en las instalaciones de la empresa Azvi , a la que Aldama vinculó con el pago de comisiones a cambio de adjudicaciones . En concreto, el comisionista apuntaba a un pago de 18.000 euros realizado en octubre de 2019 a la empresa Pilot Club Natación de Sevilla que en realidad era una compensación por la obra pública adjudicada gracias a su mediación en Transportes.

Durante la operación policial realizada este jueves, los agentes detuvieron a la pareja de Ábalos, Andrea de la Torre, y a los hermanos Corvillo, así como a otros tres empresarios. Cristian Corvillo, que realizó labores de chófer del PSOE, declaró el pasado septiembre como testigo ante el juez de la Audiencia Nacional Santiago Pedraz, instructor del caso del fraude del IVA en hidrocarburos, que se había reunido con el exministro de Transportes por asuntos relacionados con el partido socialista, ya que era su secretario de Organización, y que tanto él como su hermano Rubén tuvieron vínculos con el conseguidor Víctor de Aldama, aunque, según su versión, los negocios nunca fructificaron.

sources.headline: Koldo García asegura que acordó con el abogado del PP un millón de euros a cambio de información para hacer caer a Sánchez

sources.body:
Koldo García, exassessor de José Luis Ábalos, exministre de Transports, ha explicat que l' advocat del PP, Alberto Durán, li va oferir un milió d'euros i reduir-li la condemna a canvi d' informació per derrocar el govern de Pedro Sánchez.

En uns àudios enviats a la Cadena SER des de la presó, Koldo ha explicat que el pagament d'aquesta suma s'havia de fer a través del director d'OK Diario, Eduardo Inda .

En les gravacions, Koldo assegura que l'advocat li va dir que havia de donar informació que afectés Pedro Sánchez i el seu entorn, especialment la seva dona, Begoña Gómez, " encara que fos mentida" . També li demanaven que parlés sobre l'expresident José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero.

Em va plantejar una reducció de pena que hauria suposat no entrar a la presó, treure la meva família del procés, pagar la meva defensa i la quantitat d'un milió d'euros.

Durant el seu torn d'última paraula en el judici pel cas Mascaretes , en què el van condemnar a 19 anys de presó , l'exassessor ja va deixar anar que l'advocat del PP li havia dit que la seva condemna "quedaria en res" si mentia i donava informació sobre l'entorn de Sánchez.

Koldo ha explicat que va dinar amb Inda per coordinar l'acord econòmic i el contingut d'una entrevista que més tard li van acabar fent. Segons ha indicat, era conscient que aquest contingut acabaria sent una declaració davant les autoritats judicials . L'exassessor també ha afegit que les respostes de l'entrevista no van agradar prou a OK Diario, i per això no van pagar-li tot el que li havien promès.

Per la seva banda, fonts del PP mantenen que les acusacions són "absolutament falses ".

Pedro Sánchez ha dit que Alberto Núñez Feijóo "hauria de donar una explicació" davant d'aquestes "acusacions tan greus", mentre que el PSOE ha anunciat que estudia emprendre accions legals arran del testimoni de Koldo García.

La secretària d'Organització, Rebeca Torró, ha acusat el PP d'haver participat en reunions en què "hi hauria un acord amb Koldo García perquè destrossés el president del govern i el PSOE amb mentides i falsedats i a canvi cobrés un milió d'euros".

"De tot això hi ha unes factures que paga OKDiario", ha dit Torró, que ha insistit que el PP "hauria de donar explicacions". La dirigent socialista ha advertit que, si es confirma el relat, els populars haurien intentat comprar el testimoni d'un acusat per fer caure un govern legítim .

El PSOE considera que els fets serien d'una "gravetat extrema" i constituirien una operació de "guerra bruta" contra el govern espanyol.

També exigeixen saber d'on van sortir els diners amb què OKDiario va pagar la defensa de Koldo García, de la qual existeixen factures, i per què el PP va apartar Alberto Durán dels seus serveis jurídics.

Complint un requeriment de l'Audiència Nacional, l'advocada de Koldo García, Letícia de la Hoz, va presentar la setmana passada dues factures que confirmen que OK Diario va pagar 242.000 euros de la seva defensa. El jutjat va demanar les factures en el marc de la investigació del cas Leire , les presumptes estratègies del PSOE per frenar les causes judicials que afecten el partit.

stories.headline: Ibero-American summit agrees joint declaration despite many leaders’ absence

sources.body: <p>La cumbre iberoamericana de Madrid, pensada para reimpulsar un foro creado hace 35 años, constata que los lazos entre ambos lados del Atlántico siguen vivos, aunque tocados. Se han salvado en cualquier caso los muebles. La cita, con el respaldo de España como anfitriona, ha contado con la presencia de una decena de jefes de Estado y de Gobierno de los 22 países; no ha habido enfrentamientos dialécticos reseñables durante el turno de palabras de los líderes en la sesión plenaria de este jueves, más allá de un <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-05/milei-homologa-el-socialismo-con-el-fascismo-pero-evita-el-ataque-personal-contra-pedro-sanchez.html" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-05/milei-homologa-el-socialismo-con-el-fascismo-pero-evita-el-ataque-personal-contra-pedro-sanchez.html">intento del argentino Javier Milei de descerrajar su furia dialéctica contra los socialistas</a>; y las delegaciones han adoptado una declaración conjunta; aunque es un texto de mínimos. Se trata, en toco caso, de un logro si se tiene en cuenta que en la última edición en Ecuador (2024) no fueron capaces ni siquiera consensuar un comunicado que representara a todos. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-06/la-cumbre-iberoamericana-garantiza-su-continuidad-a-pesar-de-la-ausencia-de-la-mayoria-de-lideres-en-madrid.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: La Cumbre Iberoamericana garantiza su continuidad a pesar de la ausencia de la mayoría de líderes en Madrid

sources.body:
Foto de familia durante la XXX Cumbre Iberoamericana de Jefes de Estado y de Gobierno, en la Galería de Colecciones Reales, a 5 de noviembre de 2026, en Madrid (España). / Eduardo Parra - Europa Press

La buena noticia para los organizadores de la 30 Cumbre Iberoamericana de Madrid es que el formato ha recibido un espaldarazo tras el fiasco de la última cita, la de Ecuador, con solo cuatro líderes. En Madrid se han reunido los jefes de Estado y de Gobierno de 10 países y los vicepresidentes o cancilleres de los otros 12. La próxima edición será en Honduras en 2028.

La otra buena noticia es que el ambiente ha sido razonablemente distendido , monótono casi, con una excepción: la de Javier Milei. Y aun así, el presidente argentino solo ha desentonado con el tono general de concordia, pero al menos esta vez no ha atacado frontalmente al presidente del país anfitrión. En varias de sus visitas a España, Milei insultó a Pedro Sánchez, a su familia y a los votantes socialistas. En esta ocasión, se ha limitado a cargar contra las ideas socialistas y socialdemócratas , que ha igualado con las fascistas por lo que, a su parecer, es un uso del Estado para reprimir las libertades individuales. Este miércoles no acudió a la recepción que ofreció el Rey Felipe VI en el Teatro Real. Pedro Sánchez ha preferido no responderle: "El insulto no forma parte de mi forma de hacer política"

Hacía frío en Madrid en la mañana de este jueves mientras el ministro de Exteriores, José Manuel Albares , esperaba para ir recibiendo a los líderes en el exterior de la Galería de las Colecciones Reales , el lugar de la cita, junto al Palacio Real de la capital. Frío fue el saludo de Albares a Milei ("pasa por aquí, gracias") y frío también el que dio Milei a Sánchez; ni siquiera un segundo de apretón de manos y mirada perdida .

Era esta una cumbre de líderes eminentemente conservadores o ultraderechistas, a la que han faltado pesos pesados de la izquierda , como la mexicana Claudia Sheinbaum o el brasileño Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva. Y eso se ha notado en los discursos. No solo en las referencias constantes a Dios de muchos de los ponentes. También en el fondo de algunas cuestiones: la nueva presidenta de Costa Rica, Laura Fernández, por ejemplo, ha defendido su política de mano dura contra el narcotráfico. Costa Rica acaba de construir una cárcel inspirada en el controvertido modelo salvadoreño de Nayib Bukele. Más conciliador ha sido el presidente chileno, el ultraderechista José Antonio Kast , que ha llamado a superar las diferencias históricas de la región mediante una cooperación centrada en resultados.

Las mayores divergencias, sin embargo, han llegado al final.

Cuatro países se han desmarcado del punto cuatro de la Declaración de Madrid, el texto final de la cumbre: Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica y Paraguay . El apartado dice: " Rechazamos la coerción y la aplicación de medidas contrarias al Derecho Internacional y la Carta de las Naciones Unidas que obstaculicen la capacidad de los Estados para hacer frente a sus necesidades y prioridades en materia de desarrollo". Los cuatro países han dejado constancia expresa de que no suscriben este punto, aunque el documento no explica los motivos de su discrepancia.

sources.body: (ACN/Redacció) Dimecres, 11 de novembre, hi ha convocada una vaga general de 24 hores i ja es comencen a perfilar quins seran els serveis mínims durant l’aturada que ha decretat el Departament d’Empresa i Treball. Les afectacions més rellevants seran al transport públic, que garantirà un 25 % de servei en hores punta, mentre les urgències es mantenen en funcionament normal i a les escoles hi haurà un docent per cada sis aules a infantil i primària. Quines afectacions té el transport? Rodalies, el metro, els Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat (FGC), el tramvia i els autobusos urbans i interurbans hauran de garantir el 25 % del servei habitual durant les hores punta . Això comprèn les hores entre les 6.30 i les 9.30 h, i de les 16.30 h a les 21 h. En canvi, el servei d’autobús que connecta Barcelona amb l’aeroport funcionarà al 50 % durant tota la jornada. També et pot interessar Drets i deures dels treballadors per la vaga de l’11 de novembre: sou, serveis mínims i piquets Clara Aliaguilla 2 minuts de lectura A més, el transport de mercaderies també tindrà serveis mínims per abastir els establiments sanitaris i les farmàcies. Quina atenció hi haurà als centres sanitaris? Durant la jornada de vaga es manté el funcionament normal de les urgències , unitats especials (UCI, coronàries, diàlisi, parts) i el transport sanitari urgent. El Departament d'Empresa i Treball ha decretat aquest dijous els serveis mínims per la vaga de l'onze de novembre , convocada per dimecres de la setmana vinent.

Pel que fa al transport públic, estableix el 25% en el servei habitual a Rodalies, Ferrocarrils, metro, tramvia i autobusos urbans i interurbans durant les hores punta, de les 6.30 h a les 9.30 h i de les 16.30 h a les 21.00 h. L'ordre diu que s'ha de garantir el funcionament normal d'urgències , unitats especials (UCI, coronàries, diàlisi, parts) i el transport sanitari urgent. L'atenció primària funcionarà amb un 25% de la plantilla o el dispositiu d'atenció continuada corresponent. També es manté el servei de les farmàcies de guàrdia.

En l'àmbit de l'ensenyamen t, als centres educatius no universitaris i llars d'infants es fixa la presència d'una persona de l'equip directiu, a més de percentatges específics de docents i personal de menjador per assegurar la vigilància i seguretat dels infants. En el cas de primària es fixa un docent per cada sis unitats, a l'educació especial el 50% de la plantilla, a les llars d'infants el 33% i per garantir la seguretat en l'horari de menjador i activitats complementàries el 33%.

En el cas de les emergències i la seguretat , l'edicte estipula que els serveis d'atenció telefònica d'urgències (com ara el 112), l'extinció d'incendis i la seguretat en subministraments bàsics (aigua, llum, gas) mantindran dotacions d'entre el 70% i el 85% de les plantilles, segons l'àmbit, "per protegir la vida i la salut pública".

Als mitjans de comunicació, la ràdio i televisió públiques hauran d'emetre el 50% dels continguts informatius habituals, i hauran de garantir, en tot cas, els avisos d'emergència que es poguessin produir.

L'ordre també estableix serveis mínims per a altres àrees, com el transport de mercaderies, que serà "l'imprescindible" per abastir els establiments sanitaris i les farmàcies i per transportar les de naturalesa perible que no siguin susceptibles de conservació més enllà de 24 hores.

També n'hi ha, per exemple, per als serveis funeraris, amb un 85% del de recollida de difunts i un 50% del d'administració i d'atenció als familiars.

stories.headline: Barcelona advances plan to curb speculative home purchases

sources.body:
Una dona mira anuncis en una immobiliària. | JESÚS PRIETO / Zowy Voeten / EPC

El pleno del Ayuntamiento de Barcelona ha aprobado este jueves una proposición presentada por Barcelona en Comú para reforzar las medidas contra la compra especulativa de viviendas y avanzar en la protección del mercado residencial de la ciudad. La iniciativa ha salido adelante con los votos favorables de PSC, Barcelona en Comú y ERC , mientras que Junts per Barcelona, PP y Vox han votado en contra.

El acuerdo insta al gobierno municipal de Jaume Collboni a velar "de manera contundente" por el cumplimiento del Real Decreto-ley 29/2026, de 6 de octubre , que establece medidas urgentes para proteger la función social de la vivienda y ampliar la oferta de vivienda asequible frente a determinadas prácticas especulativas.

La proposición también reclama que el Ayuntamiento inicie los trabajos preliminares para modificar el planeamiento urbanístico , con el objetivo de que Barcelona se convierta en la primera ciudad de Catalunya en aplicar la prohibición de las compras especulativas , una vez se apruebe la legislación autonómica correspondiente.

Uno de los principales puntos de la iniciativa es exigir al consistorio que refuerce los mecanismos de control para garantizar el cumplimiento de la normativa estatal sobre la adquisición de viviendas por parte de determinados grandes tenedores y entidades dedicadas a operaciones inmobiliarias.

El artículo 1 del Real Decreto-ley 29/2026 establece, hasta el 31 de diciembre de 2030 , limitaciones a determinadas adquisiciones de viviendas por parte de grandes tenedores y entidades inmobiliarias cuando se realizan por un importe inferior al 70% de su valor de mercado , con las excepciones previstas en la normativa.

Con esta propuesta, Barcelona en Comú pretende que el Ayuntamiento adopte las medidas necesarias para supervisar el cumplimiento de estas restricciones y reforzar la protección del parque residencial frente a las operaciones especulativas.

Además, el texto aprobado establece que el gobierno municipal deberá presentar un informe trimestral en el que se detallen las actuaciones realizadas para garantizar el cumplimiento de la normativa y los resultados obtenidos.

Este seguimiento periódico permitirá conocer qué medidas ha puesto en marcha el Ayuntamiento y cuáles han sido sus resultados , con el objetivo de evaluar su aplicación en el mercado inmobiliario barcelonés.

Otro de los aspectos destacados del acuerdo es el apoyo del Ayuntamiento a la aprobación, con la máxima rapidez, de la ley catalana para prohibir las compras especulativas , actualmente en tramitación en el Parlament de Catalunya.

La propuesta pretende poner límites a la acumulación de viviendas en manos de fondos de inversión y grandes tenedores , una de las cuestiones que Barcelona en Comú considera prioritarias para afrontar las dificultades de acceso a la vivienda.

En este sentido, el pleno ha acordado instar al gobierno municipal a comenzar los trabajos necesarios para adaptar el planeamiento urbanístico de la ciudad a las futuras restricciones.

stories.headline: Barcelona approves public company to rehabilitate homes in Besòs-Maresme

sources.body: El Plenari de l’Ajuntament de Barcelona ha aprovat inicialment la creació de l’empresa pública Impulsem Futur Besòs-Maresme, SA (constituïda de forma mixta entre l’Ajuntament i la Generalitat), que serà l’encarregada de fer la rehabilitació de centenars de pisos que ara mateix estan en un estat deplorable al barri del Besòs i el Maresme . A llarg termini, l’empresa mixta es proposa rehabilitar 4.000 pisos fins al 2038, amb una inversió total de 415 M€ . Ara bé, en una primera fase , el Plenari ha aprovat una inversió municipal de 50 M€ fins al 2029, als quals caldrà sumar 45 M€ que hi aportarà el govern català. Per tant, la regeneració del Besòs i el Maresme s’ha garantit ara 95 M€ de pressupost entre el 2026 i el 2029 . Al plenari, la creació d’Impulsem Futur Besòs-Maresme, SA, ha rebut el suport del PSC del govern, de Junts, de BComú (amb qui es va pactar aquest pla de regeneració urbana a llarg termini) i d’ERC. En canvi, el PP i Vox s’han abstingut. També et pot interessar Ajuntament i Generalitat encarrilen la regeneració del Besòs: 415 M€ per rehabilitar 4.000 pisos Jaume Planagumà Marina Segura i Vidal 2 minuts de lectura Salt d’escala en un deute històric La tinenta d’alcaldia d’Urbanisme, Laia Bonet , ha defensat que es farà “ un salt d’escala ” perquè, fins ara, en quatre anys s’han rehabilitat només 192 pisos i “aquest ritme no ens el podem permetre”. Damià Calvet ( Junts ) ha demanat responsabilitat i ha donat suport a l’empresa pública “pensant en els veïns del Besòs”, mentre que Tània Corrons ( BComú ) ha lamentat que “la ciutat i el país tenen un deute històric amb el veïnat del barri, des dels anys 60″. Eva Baró ( ERC ) ha qualificat l’acord com “un pas molt important” i ha confiat que marcarà “ un abans i un després “, mentre que Víctor Martí ( PP ) ha avisat que “una nova empresa no garanteix que les obres arribin abans ” i Liberto Senderos ( Vox ) ha denunciat que “quan queden 24 dies per a les eleccions generals 2026, ens venen la solució del segle “. El menjador d’un dels pisos amb problemes estructurals greus, que necessita estar completament estintolat Hi haurà enderrocs? La creació de l’empresa mixta arriba enmig del neguit que tenen els veïns del Besòs i el Maresme, que tenen por que es facin enderrocs . Aquesta temença neix de l’informe tècnic que es va encarregar previ a la constitució de l’empresa pública: el document plantejava un escenari que requeria tirar a terra 1.800 pisos (quasi la meitat dels 4.000 afectats pel pla de regeneració urbana). La preocupació pels possibles enderrocs també l’ha traslladada al plenari la regidora Corrons, dels comuns. Ara bé, la tinenta d’alcaldia Bonet ha estat taxativa: “Quan es crea una empresa pública, els informes han d’analitzar tots els escenaris possibles… i analitzar un escenari no vol dir escollir-lo . Les decisions polítiques les prenem tots plegats”. També et pot interessar L’oposició reprova Laia Bonet per les rehabilitacions del Besòs i el Maresme Jaume Planagumà 1 minut de lectura
sources.headline: Barcelona crea una empresa pública per rehabilitar el Besòs: ara per ara, 95 M€ fins al 2029

sources.body:
El portal del bloque situado en el número dos de la calle Alfons el Magnànim, en el barrio del Besòs i el Maresme, en Barcelona. / MANU MITRU

El Ayuntamiento de Barcelona ha dado luz verde este jueves al convenio con la Generalitat de Catalunya para crear una sociedad pública destinada a impulsar la rehabilitación urbanística del Besòs-Maresme. La iniciativa, que contempla una inversión de 415 millones de euros durante los próximos diez años y actuaciones en 4.000 viviendas , ha salido adelante con los votos favorables del PSC, Junts, Barcelona en Comú y ERC, mientras que PP y Vox se han abstenido.

La nueva empresa, denominada Impulsem Futur Besòs-Maresme, SA , será el instrumento encargado de desarrollar las actuaciones previstas en esta zona de la ciudad. Según el acuerdo, la Generalitat aportará 150 millones de euros a lo largo de una década, mientras que el Ayuntamiento asumirá los 265 millones restantes. Como primera fase, ambas administraciones prevén movilizar unos 95 millones de euros hasta 2029.

La primera teniente de alcaldía, Laia Bonet , ha defendido que la iniciativa permitirá dar un "salto de escala" en la rehabilitación de viviendas y acelerar unas intervenciones que hasta ahora han avanzado a un ritmo insuficiente. Bonet ha recordado que en los últimos cuatro años únicamente se han rehabilitado 192 pisos y ha advertido de que, manteniendo ese ritmo, se necesitarían más de cuatro décadas para completar las actuaciones previstas.

La responsable municipal también ha destacado que el proyecto es fruto de los acuerdos alcanzados durante los últimos meses con Junts, ERC y los Comuns, formaciones que han coincidido en la necesidad de acelerar la transformación de estos barrios.

Los tres grupos que han respaldado el acuerdo junto al PSC han celebrado la aprobación del convenio, aunque han planteado distintas condiciones y prioridades para su desarrollo.

Desde Junts, el concejal Damià Calvet ha cuestionado la gestión de las relaciones con el vecindario durante los últimos años y ha considerado que ha faltado "mano izquierda" a la hora de trabajar con los residentes afectados por las actuaciones urbanísticas.

Por su parte, la concejala de Barcelona en Comú Tània Corrons ha advertido de que la nueva sociedad pública debe garantizar que los vecinos puedan permanecer en sus hogares. En este sentido, ha reclamado que el proyecto no se convierta en un instrumento para derribar edificios, sino que priorice la rehabilitación y la permanencia de los residentes.

La concejala de ERC Eva Baró también ha valorado positivamente el acuerdo y ha pedido que las obras se adelanten "lo más rápido posible" para dar respuesta a las necesidades de los barrios.

El convenio ha salido adelante sin el apoyo de PP y Vox, que han optado por la abstención y han expresado sus dudas sobre la planificación de las actuaciones y el calendario previsto.

El concejal del PP Víctor Martí ha criticado que la propuesta "llega tarde" y establece unos "plazos excesivamente largos". También ha reprochado al gobierno municipal que no haya detallado cuáles serán las intervenciones urgentes ni qué criterios se seguirán para establecer las prioridades.

sources.body:
L’Ajuntament de Barcelona rectificarà i les dues pròximes convocatòries de Bonus Cultura que llançarà es restringiran a ciutadans empadronats a la capita catalana. “Es demanarà la residència certificada”, ha dit el regidor de Cultura, Xavier Marcé . Aquest dijous, el consistori va oferir 20 euros per persona en 20.000 bonus culturals. Els ajuts es van esgotar en menys de 24 hores, però al voltant d’un 20% del total ha anat a parar a mans de ciutadans de fora de Barcelona, segons les dades facilitades per l’Ajuntament. El fet que la convocatòria s’ha obert a tot Catalunya ha estat criticada per ERC.

Els Bonus cultura van ser una proposta d’@ERCbcn de 2024. Un bonus adreçat a barcelonins per gaudir de la cultura en català. El govern de BCN obre la convocatòria i la fa per a tot Catalunya?! i s’han exhaurit ja. Deixant barcelonins fora de la sol•licitud, esclar. Sort que aquests eren els qui sabien gestionar.

La presidenta d’ERC a l’Ajuntament i alcaldable, Elisenda Alamany , ha recordat que la proposta dels Bonus Cultura va ser dels republicans i ha denunciat que si s’han esgotat tan ràpidament ha estat deixant fora a ciutadans de Barcelona. “Sort que aquests eren els qui sabien gestionar”, ha dit Alamany en referència a l’executiu socialista de Jaume Collboni.

Altres problemes detectats en la tramitació dels bonus són que el web es va col·lapsar i els gmails donaven error.

A mitja tarda d’aquest dijous, l’Ajuntament ha emès una nota de premsa en la qual destacava que els 20.000 Bonus Cultura s’havien exhaurit en un dia. Posteriorment, arran de les crítiques d’ERC, el regidor de Cultura ha anunciat que les dues convocatòries vinents, previstes de l’11 de gener al 25 d’abril i del 26 d’abril al 31 de juliol, es destinaran només a ciutadans de la capital de Catalunya. Seran 35.000 bonus, fins a arribar als 55.000 totals, amb una dotació pressupostària d’1,5 milions d’euros.

En la seva compareixença, Marcé ha assegurat que el 80% dels 20.000 bonus oferts han anat a mans de barcelonins; el 15%, a veïns de l’àrea metropolitana, i la resta, a gent d’altres punts de Catalunya. El regidor de Cultura ha valorat la convocatòria com un èxit, ja que els ajuts s’han acabat en 15 hores.

Els ajuts funcionen amb un moneder precarregat amb 20 euros per a cada usuari que està integrat amb els principals sistemes de venda d’entrades mitjançant una eina tecnològica que no altera els canals habituals dels programadors. Per a sol·licitar l’ajut en les pròximes convocatòries, la persona haurà d’entrar en el web dels bonus de l’Ajuntament. Els bonus es poden fer servir per a espectacles d’arts en viu, cinema en català i compra de llibres. La proposta incorpora el criteri de priorització del català, amb el 70% de l’oferta per a cultura en aquesta llengua.
